rated_messages.input_message: Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.

Think about what is really important to you. Maybe it's spending time with family or a friend, exercising, doing something spiritual, or creating something. Whatever it is, take a step in that direction.

Recent research has found that people who use self-talk when they try not to smoke (e.g. telling yourself 'you can do it') are more successful than people who don't. It might seem a bit strange, but talking to yourself like this appears to really help.
Take a deep breath. Focus on today and the things you have accomplished. How many urges have you let pass? Give yourself some credit!
Step back from what is stressful by taking 10 slow breaths. Count them as you go and notice your breath. If you get distracted, keep starting over until you get to 10.
Ways of dealing with urges: play a game or an online quiz.
If you find yourself with a few minutes to spare, it can be nice to read back over old messages. It's also a chance to reply to ones that you might have forgotten about!

Write down why you want to stop smoking to resist a craving. Remember, trying something to beat the urge is always better than doing nothing. Each time you resist a cig, you're one step closer to being tobacco-free.
Keep picturing yourself getting home later today knowing that you've gained a smoke-free day. It's nearly a reality!
Think about times in the past when you have let urges pass during a stressful moment, and notice what helped make that moment easier.
